subject: Is your eval layer as strong as your engagement stat?
text:
Hi [NAME],

From the research I've done, [COMPANY]'s agent teams close care gaps, verify coverage, and book appointments in one coordinated workflow.

The agentic AI infrastructure is strong. The gap most teams in this position hit is the human review layer, a systematic way to catch agent output errors before they reach members, and an audit trail that satisfies payer compliance requirements.

We work with healthcare and enterprise AI teams on that layer, including Appfolio and Synthesia on text and document workflows.

Without it:

• 
Agent failures compound silently before member impact.

• 
Payer audits surface gaps in model output traceability.

Worth 20 minutes this week to show what that setup looks like?

subject: One surgeon, two rooms - the data layer
text:
Hi [NAME],

Yossi's post in February describes the end goal: one surgeon on a complex decompression in Room A, Dynamis executing routine bone milling autonomously in Room B. More patients treated, same surgical workforce.

Getting there means training a new autonomous capability for every new procedure step. Each one needs an annotated operating room video from real cases. That annotation step sits between every completed procedure and every new training run.

The pattern we see at teams your size: the engineers building the models are also manually deciding what to annotate. At 10 cases a month, it is fine, but at 50 it becomes the bottleneck.

We work with Moon Surgical on exactly this & I thought it would be worth a 20-minute call next Thursday afternoon? Let me know.

subject: When the model gets it wrong, the member calls
text:
Hi [NAME],

Your payer customers sell [COMPANY] on member engagement and care gap closure. Both depend on your SLMs getting the recommendation right.

The gap most AI-first teams hit at your scale is knowing whether the model is working before it ships and being able to show that to a payer under HITRUST audit.

We work with Synthesia and Appfolio on that evaluation and curation layer. Teams come to us when model iteration is the priority and building evaluation infrastructure internally is slowing it down.

If relevant, do you have 20 minutes this Thursday to see if there is a parallel?

subject: EU AI Act and 9 cardiac indications
text:
Hi [NAME],

the EU AI Act which comes into force in August requires a documented record
of who labelled what for every model update. As i understand, MyCardium
runs 9 indications across two cleared products, which if my math is
correct, is nine separate records to keep current.

The gap is usually the paper trail behind it, which teams struggle with.
We work with abbvie and Conavi Medical team on annotating DICOM series
together for their FDA submission.

Thought it would be relevant to you and am happy to chat further if you're
interested.

subject: Deep Learning Hiring - 1 person 2 jobs
text:
Hi [NAME], 

I saw the Deep Learning Research Engineer role. "Improve our data pipeline" next to "train models" usually means one person doing two jobs?!

We work with teams hitting the same wall, labelling tools built for bounding boxes break down on person-crop embeddings, where identity ambiguity makes every annotation decision harder. 

Automotus had 30,000 images, mostly near-duplicates, no fast way to find them. Embedding-based curation got them to ~10,000, no accuracy loss.

What's eating more of your time right now, models or data pipeline? Would have to chat more if you're free.

subject: line in your ReID post that caught my eye
text:
Hi [NAME],

Saw the two Deep Learning Engineer openings referencing "improve our data pipeline" and "build datasets" alongside model training. Guessing your engineers are still maintaining the labelling infrastructure?

That tends to slow teams down right when they need to move fastest, especially post-Series A. 

Tooling built for one detection task rarely stretches to the next, so every new hire spends part of their ramp rebuilding the pipeline instead of training models.

We saw the same at Automotus. Embedding-based curation cut their 30,000-image dataset to ~10,000 with no accuracy loss, and freed the engineers to get back to model work.

Love the blog, by the way. If you're interested, it would be great to grab 20 minutes to chat later this week?

text:

I saw the world ploughing record at Birch Farm last year in May. I hope you still have the record, it's extremely cool - I grew up on a farm and love to see the technology in this field progressing!

We work with agricultural robotics teams, including John Deere on one specific problem: closing the gap between the data the machines log in the field and data that actually improves the model.

As the fleet continues to double, that gap tends to widen faster than the team. 

Do you have 20 minutes next Thursday at 2 pm to see if we can help?

subject: AgBot T2 Doubling Problem
text:
Hi [NAME], 

We just started working with John Deere on similar autonomous field robot perception use cases as agXeed, so I thought I'd reach out.

Motion engineers in the agricultural robotics space come to us when:

• 

Field incident logs have no automated filter - engineers manually decide which obstacle events are worth pulling into a training dataset.

• 

Annotating LiDAR and camera captures from real field conditions requires a setup that general-purpose tools weren't built for.

• 

The loop from a field failure to a corrected labelled example in the retraining queue takes weeks, not days.

Do you face similar issues at agXeed?

If so, it might be worth having an initial conversation to see whether our offerings fit your needs. I'm free next Wednesday at 2pm.
